candidate.title: EpiRADSeq
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina EpiRADseq schematic, from genomic DNA through restriction digestion, barcoded adapters, a depicted second HpaII digest, P2 addition and amplification to DNA. The drawn route is preserved; Schield et al. clarifies the methylation-sensitive readout and corrects the actual implementation to digestion with PstI and HpaII before adapter ligation. ddRADseq is the named parent subprotocol in the caption, not a separately depicted alternative target. No unshown MspI adaptation, pooling, size-selection or sequencing operation is added.

states.label: Amplified DNA library
features: Final panel is labeled DNA and shows multiple blue lines. Colored adapters are no longer rendered; this does not depict a separate removal reaction.
The sequenced carrier is genomic DNA library fragments, with adapter barcodes associating fragments with samples. Sequencing itself is reported by the paper but is not a drawn operation.
Across samples, locus presence/absence and relative read depth are used to infer the frequency of unmethylated HpaII sites: greater relative locus recovery indicates lower methylation at that site.

The readout is reduced representation, averaged over sampled cells and DNA strands; it does not exhaustively map genomic methylation or resolve homo- versus hemi-methylation. Absence of reads is not by itself proof of methylation: genetic changes in restriction sites can also prevent locus recovery.

operations.label: Restriction digestion
operations.description: Restriction-site-marked genomic DNA is cleaved into genomic fragments that provide the substrate for adapter addition. The unadapted intermediate is implied rather than separately drawn. The diagram leaves the first enzyme unnamed.
operations.mechanism: Restriction-enzyme cleavage. In the primary EpiRADseq implementation, PstI and HpaII digestion precede adapter ligation; this differs from the diagram's staged order.
operations.information_effect: Restricts the genomic material to restriction-defined fragments; the actual EpiRADseq double digest also makes recovery depend on HpaII-site methylation.

operations.label: Second restriction digest with methylation-sensitive HpaII
operations.description: The diagram places HpaII after barcoded adapter addition and shows shorter products that retain one original adapter/barcode end. For the chemistry and biological interpretation, the primary source establishes HpaII-site methylation-dependent locus recovery; it places HpaII with PstI before adapter ligation, rather than validating this post-ligation digest. The drawn input history and outputs are retained here as schematic observations, not a verified staged protocol.
operations.mechanism: HpaII recognizes CCGG; methylation-sensitive failure to cut prevents recovery of the corresponding EpiRADseq locus. This mechanism is taken from the primary source, with the order discrepancy recorded in c_digest_order.
operations.information_effect: Transfers information about restriction-site methylation into the abundance of recoverable genomic loci. Methylated-site molecules do not provide the corresponding cut-defined locus; fragment recovery is not proof that the entire DNA molecule is unmethylated.

corrections.diagram_observation: The diagram orders Restriction digestion, Add barcoded adapters, Second restriction digest with methylation-sensitive HpaII, Add P2 adapter, then Amplify. Adapter-bearing long fragments become shorter one-adapter fragments at the second digest.
corrections.primary_statement: Schield et al., EpiRADseq library preparation, reports PstI and HpaII digestion first, then ligation of double-stranded sequencing adapters with unique barcodes, followed by size selection and amplification. Thus the supplied full text resolves the actual implementation order as both restriction enzymes acting before adapter ligation. It does not support the drawn second post-ligation HpaII digest or a separately described subsequent P2-addition step. op_hpai uses the primary-supported methylation-sensitive mechanism and readout while preserving the drawn route as an explicitly qualified illustration.

unknowns.question: Which enzyme is intended specifically for the diagram's unnamed first Restriction digestion stage? The primary implementation uses PstI with HpaII before ligation, but does not independently assign PstI to this drawn staged input history. Resolving the illustrator's exact staged intent would require a figure-specific legend or protocol; the schematic architecture and primary correction do not depend on that assignment.

Does a separate EpiRADseq implementation support this exact adapter-before-HpaII and subsequent P2 route? The assigned image depicts it, but the supplied primary full text reports a different order. A figure-specific source describing that staged interface would be needed to establish it as an executable implementation; this record retains it only at schematic scope.
